Subject: Pilot scoping: enforce single model variant + US-only routing

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot conversation is moving quickly on our side. We need to lock a couple of technical and contractual items before we start ingesting PHI-labeled test data:

1) Variant enforcement: OptiHealth requires that the pilot traffic be served by a single, audited model variant (no automatic fallback to other variants or cheaper quantized snapshots).
2) Geo-isolation: All inference must remain in the US (no cross-region routing).
3) Data handling: We will provide a SOC2 excerpt and expect audit logs for token-level access during the pilot.

We attached a draft mutual action plan (pilot-MAP.xlsx) and a signed confidentiality opt-in (opt-in-docusign.pdf). Can Redwood confirm feasibility (technical + cost) and a proposed delivery timeline?

If you need a legal contact for our side, loop in me and our security team (security@optihealth.com). Tight timeline: we hope to begin test traffic the week of Sep 21.

Thanks,
Alice Huang
Head of Integrations, OptiHealth

Alice — thanks for the clear asks and the MAP. Forwarding to product/security/ops for feasibility checks (cc'd).

Quick internal checklist so we have a common frame:
- Enforced single-variant: confirm whether you need a specific model commit SHA / quantization profile pinned.
- No-fallback: do you require that the platform never fall back under any capacity pressure, or is a controlled fallback with explicit notification acceptable?
- Geo-lock: US-only region is straightforward for hosted customers, but we need to confirm whether Dedicated (reserved pool) is required to guarantee it under surge.

Karthik / Monica / Lauren — can you weigh in on technical constraints, recommended architecture (hosted with pinned variant vs. dedicated pool), impact to latency/cost, and a short rollout plan? If dedicated capacity is required, we should flag procurement and capacity lead times.

I'll send OptiHealth a brief summary once we have tradeoffs.

—Markus

On Wed, Sep 2, 2026 at 08:15 AM Alice Huang <alice.huang@optihealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot conversation is moving quickly on our side. We need to lock a couple of technical and contractual items before we start ingesting PHI-labeled test data:
> 1) Variant enforcement: OptiHealth requires that the pilot traffic be served by a single, audited model variant (no automatic fallback to other variants or cheaper quantized snapshots).
> 2) Geo-isolation: All inference must remain in the US (no cross-region routing).

Thanks for the clear asks. Technical assessment and recommended approach below.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Provision a small Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) in US-East and pin the exact model binary/quantization profile there.
- Disable automatic model fallback for routes associated with the pilot and configure explicit failover to a manual standby (no automated downgrade).
- Enable extended audit logging and export of KV cache/trace events to a secured Customer Drive location.

Tradeoffs / constraints:
- Throughput & cost: Dedicated pinned instances lower variability (good) but increase committed cost. If OptiHealth needs burst coverage beyond the pool, we can add controlled burst with manual approval.
- No-fallback: Prevents graceful degradation — when capacity saturates, requests will queue or be rate-limited. We'll need an explicit SLO (e.g., max queue time or error budget) in the MAP.
- Implementation effort: ~2 sprints (2 engineers, infra + runtime), plus 1 week for capacity provisioning and legal/contract updates.

Reqs from OptiHealth to proceed:
- Confirm model variant identifier (commit SHA + quantization profile).
- Provide SOC2 excerpt (we need the relevant controls) — already attached, thank you; our security team will review.
- Sign a temporary exception addendum that defines no-fallback behavior and accepted SLOs.

I created INF-4521 to track the work (see link) — I'll scope tasks and drop a short rollout calendar by EOD tomorrow.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product (Serving Runtime), Redwood Inference

Looping in briefly with next steps and an internal decision:

1) Approval: I approve a time-limited exception for the pilot to enforce a single model variant and US-only routing, provided we include clear acceptance criteria in the MAP and get signoff from Security & Legal.
2) Action items (owners):
   - CS (Markus) to finalize MAP with OptiHealth and capture SLOs on queue time/error budget.
   - Product (Karthik) to deliver a rollout plan and low-level infra changes (INF-4521) and estimate resource needs.
   - Security (Monica) to complete SOC2 control review and confirm audit log exports are sufficient.
   - Legal to prepare a 90-day exception addendum (procurement to be notified).

3) Capacity: If Dedicated capacity is required, Ops needs a 2-week lead to provision and reserve GPUs. Propose we treat this as a scoped pilot commit and bill as a short-term reserved pool.

Markus — once Security confirms the SOC2 excerpt (Monica), please send a one-page acceptance checklist to OptiHealth and request the exact model identifier. We should also add a clause that the exception expires after the pilot unless extended by mutual written agreement.

Thanks — keep me posted on any blockers.

—Lauren
